properties.statement: SMALL, CHEAP SURFACE FRICTIONS — TWO REAL, ONE DISPROVEN BY MEASUREMENT. (1) REAL: `add_contributor` TAKES THE HANDLE AS `id` WHILE `claim_region` TAKES THE SAME HANDLE AS `contributor_id`. w-08baa598 passed `contributor_id` to add_contributor first — because that is the field name the very next call in the documented sequence uses — and got `failed to deserialize parameters: unknown field 'contributor_id', expected one of 'id', 'name', 'kind', 'handle', 'description'`. Cost one round trip. THE ERROR MESSAGE IS GOOD and is why this is minor: it named the accepted fields. The two calls are adjacent steps in the fleet's prescribed worker sequence and the asymmetry carries no meaning. FIX SHAPE: accept `contributor_id` as an alias on add_contributor. (2) ~~`set_verification_kind` ECHOES THE PRE-UPDATE `status`~~ — **DISPROVEN HERE 2026-08-08 BY RUNNING IT, AND THIS ENTRY NOW EXISTS TO RECORD THAT.** Four seats reported it across two days (w-ec25cf2c, w-3f408ab0, sb-boss ab2291fa as 'two workers and I'), and their fleet adopted a standing habit of re-reading every node rather than trusting any echo. THE ECHO IS CORRECT. Probe: create a Verification, `set_verification_status(passing)` FIRST, then `set_verification_kind(validation)` — the ordering that would expose a stale read. The echo returned `status: passing, kind: validation` and a `get_node` returned exactly the same. `verify.rs:169-175` reads the existing node, copies every property except `kind`, and returns what `create_node` wrote; `git log -L` dates that loop to 9073b9e, 2026-07-22, the commit that introduced `Verification.kind` — so it has been correct since the feature existed and was never stale, including on the day they filed. WHAT THEY ACTUALLY SAW: they called set_verification_kind while the status genuinely still WAS `planned`, set it to `passing` afterwards, and read the earlier echo as though it described the later state. The echo described the node at the moment of that call, correctly. THE FINDING IS NOW ABOUT REPORTING, NOT ABOUT THE ECHO, and it cuts two ways. Their file's no-dedup rule exists so a maintainer can see RECURRENCE — 'one report reads as one seat's opinion while two reads as the tool doing it to everyone' — and here it turned one misreading into four, which read as strong evidence and was not. RECURRENCE IS NOT CORROBORATION WHEN THE SEATS SHARE A METHOD. And I recorded the four reproductions as strengthening the case before testing it, which is the same credulity one layer along; rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party exists for exactly this. THEIR HABIT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION AND IS STILL RIGHT: re-reading a node after a write that matters is what AGENTS.md asks for anyway. Only the stated reason was wrong. (3) REAL: `claim_region`'s TWO REFUSALS ARE BOTH CORRECT AND NEITHER NAMES ITS OWN FIX. It needs `seat` on the sessionless transport and refuses otherwise; it also needs a Contributor to exist first, failing with `Node not found: Contributor <handle>`. Both are documented — IN THE TOOL DESCRIPTIONS, which an agent only reads if it happens to load that tool. THE COST WAS NOT ONE RETRY. A worker hit the second refusal, concluded the tool was broken, and wrote 'there is NO mint_seat tool in the served surface' INTO THE WORKER ONBOARDING FILE — a false correction that TRAVELLED FIVE HOPS and reached a boss offering to amend PROTOCOL on it, before another worker disproved it with one command. FIX SHAPE: make the refusals name their own fix — 'call add_contributor first' / 'call mint_seat and pass it as seat'. NOTE THE FAMILY RESEMBLANCE to fact:defect-a-deferred-tool-reads-as-a-nonexistent-one AND to (2) above: in all three a session's reasonable inference about the tool was written down and propagated, and in two of them the inference was false. The expensive failure in this channel is not the tools — it is a conclusion travelling faster than a test.
